steps: 1) Open the demographics program of the AI kit (system.file('ai/kit/04_example_demographics.R', package = 'rtfreporter')); set output_path to a new folder and report_name to the case id, then run it. 2) Open the RTF in Word.
expected: One column per arm in the order Placebo, Xanomeline Low Dose, Xanomeline High Dose, then Total; every header shows (N=xx) with the arm's number of subjects. Visual check.

steps: 1) Use the RTF of UAT-001. 2) Compare each statistic with a summary computed independently from the same ADSL (pharmaverseadam::adsl, SAFFL == 'Y') (for example with base R aggregate()).
expected: Every n, mean, SD, median, quartile, minimum, maximum and percentage equals the independent summary, with the decimals the program declares.

steps: 1) Use the RTF of UAT-001. 2) Compare the p-value column with cardx::ard_stats_kruskal_test() / ard_stats_chisq_test() run on the same ADSL.
expected: The p-value column shows each test's p-value on its variable's first row, as the ARD gives it (<0.001 below 0.001).

steps: 1) Open the adverse events program of the AI kit (system.file('ai/kit/03_example_ae_soc_pt.R', package = 'rtfreporter')); set output_path to a new folder and report_name to the case id, then run it. 2) Open the RTF in Word and page through it.
expected: The 'Subjects with at least one TEAE' row comes first; SOCs and PTs are in descending order of frequency; no page ends with a SOC row whose first PT is on the next page. Visual check.

steps: 1) Use the RTF of UAT-004. 2) Count the preferred terms at 5% or more in any arm independently from the same ADAE and ADSL (treatment-emergent, safety population; percentages of the arm's N).
expected: The table holds exactly the PTs counted independently, each under its SOC; no SOC is left without a PT.

steps: 1) Take the plan of UAT-004 and change plan_filter(p >= 0.05) to plan_filter(p >= 2) (no term passes). 2) Add plan_empty() to the plan. 3) Write the RTF and open it.
expected: Below the 'Subjects with at least one TEAE' row (kept, with its counts) one row reads 'No subjects met the criteria.' (or the text given); there is no SOC or PT row, and the column header is printed.

steps: 1) Take cards::ADAE (first 60 records). 2) table_plan(adae) |> plan_listing(listing_col('USUBJID', width = 12), listing_col('AEDECOD', width = 20), listing_col('AETERM', width = 10)) |> plan_paginate_rows(max_rows = 20) |> plan_titles('Listing 16.2.7', 'Adverse events'). 3) rtf_document() |> rtf_tables(plan) |> generate_rtfreport(file). 4) Open the RTF.
expected: AETERM text longer than its column wraps onto further lines within the column; every page holds at most 20 lines (each line of wrapped text counts, and so does the blank line after each record), and no record is split across two pages; every page repeats the column header and the two title lines. Visual check.

steps: 1) Make a ggplot2 plot of AGE by TRT01A from cards::ADSL. 2) rtf_document() |> rtf_figures(list(rtfplot(plot, width_twips = 8640L, height_twips = 5040L)), titles = c('Figure 14.2.1', 'Age by arm'), footnotes = 'Source: cards::ADSL (dummy data)') |> generate_rtfreport(file). 3) Open the RTF.
expected: The figure is on the page at the size given, the titles above and the footnote below. Visual check.

steps: 1) Use the RTF of UAT-004 (several pages). 2) Open it in Word and look at the header and footer of the first, a middle and the last page.
expected: Every page shows 'Page x of y' with x the page number and y the total; the header and footer are in the document's font. Visual check.

steps: 1) Take the plan of UAT-007 and add plan_footnotes('Source: cards::ADAE (dummy data)'). 2) rtf_document() |> rtf_tables(plan) |> generate_rtfreport(file). 3) Open the RTF and look at every page.
expected: The two title lines ('Listing 16.2.7', 'Adverse events') are above the listing and the footnote below it, on every page. Visual check.

steps: 1) In the program of UAT-001 give the age rows one statistic a row: plan_cells(continuous = c('n' = '{N:.0f}', 'Mean' = '{mean:.1f}', 'SD' = '{sd:.2f}', 'Median' = '{median:.1f}', 'Min' = '{min:.0f}', 'Max' = '{max:.0f}'), categorical = <as it is>). 2) Add plan_columns(decimal = '.values') to the plan. 3) Write the RTF and open it.
expected: In every arm column the decimal points of Mean, SD and Median line up, and the whole numbers (n, Min, Max) end where the point would be. A cell with a companion value, such as n (%), stays one cell, as ?set_decimal_split says. Visual check.

steps: 1) In the program of UAT-001 add plan_paginate_group(col = 'group', heading = '{value}') before plan_stub(). 2) rtf_document() |> rtf_tables(tbl_plan, auto_section = TRUE) |> generate_rtfreport(file). 3) Open the RTF and page through it.
expected: One section per characteristic (Age (years); Age group, n (%); Sex, n (%); Race, n (%)), each starting on a new page with its label in the page header, under the titles. Visual check.

steps: 1) Take the plan of UAT-001 and add plan_paginate_cols(every = 2, keep = 'Characteristic'), which cuts the columns as a table too wide for the page is cut. 2) Write the RTF and open it.
expected: The columns are split into blocks of two (Placebo and Xanomeline Low Dose; Xanomeline High Dose and Total; the p-value column), one block a page; every block repeats the Characteristic column and its part of the column header. Visual check.

steps: 1) In the program of UAT-001 remove {DATETIME} from the footnotes. 2) Run it twice to two files. 3) unname(tools::md5sum(c(file1, file2))) -- compare the two checksums.
expected: The two checksums are identical (byte for byte the same RTF).

steps: 1) Run the program of UAT-007 twice, to two files. 2) unname(tools::md5sum(c(file1, file2))) -- compare the two checksums.
expected: The two checksums are identical (byte for byte the same RTF).

steps: 1) Take the plan of UAT-001 and give it plan_titles('表 14.1.1 人口統計学的特性') (or any non-ASCII text your studies use). 2) Before normalize_ard(), relabel a level of SEX in the data to Japanese (for example '女性' for 'F'). 3) Write the RTF and open it.
expected: The title and the relabelled level show in Word exactly as given.

steps: 1) In the program of UAT-001 use cards::ADSL and replace the ARD with ard_stack(adsl, .by = TRT01A, .overall = TRUE, ard_tabulate(variables = DCREASCD)). 2) plan_cells(categorical = '{n:.0f} ({p:.1f%})'), plan_labels(c(DCREASCD = 'Reason for discontinuation, n (%)')), plan_levels(DCREASCD = <'Completed' first, then the reasons>). 3) Drop plan_compare() and its column: the p entries of plan_col_header() and the last width of plan_columns(). 4) Write the RTF and open it.
expected: One row per reason, 'Completed' first, n (%) under each arm and Total (a zero count prints as 0); the counts equal table(adsl$DCREASCD, adsl$TRT01A). Visual check.

steps: 1) From cards::ADAE (TRTEMFL == 'Y') flag each subject of cards::ADSL (SAFFL == 'Y'): any TEAE; AESER == 'Y'; AEREL 'POSSIBLE' or 'PROBABLE'; DSRAEFL == 'Y' in ADSL (discontinued for an adverse event); AESDTH == 'Y' (one logical column each). 2) ard_stack(adsl, .by = TRT01A, ard_tabulate_value(variables = <the five flags>)), which keeps the TRUE level only. 3) normalize_ard() |> table_plan(cols = 'TRT01A', rows = 'variable'), plan_cells('{n:.0f} ({p:.1f%})'), plan_labels() for the five rows, plan_hide('label'), plan_col_header() with (N=xx). 4) Write the RTF and open it.
expected: Five rows in the order given, each n (%) of the arm's N; the counts equal those computed independently from ADAE and ADSL. Visual check.

steps: 1) Use the adverse events program of UAT-004 with AESEV a factor (levels MILD, MODERATE, SEVERE). 2) Make three subsets of ADAE, each keeping the record of highest AESEV: one per subject, one per subject and SOC, one per subject and PT. 3) Build the ARD with ard_stack_hierarchical(by = c(TRT01A, AESEV), denominator = adsl, id = USUBJID) on each and bind_ard() them: the subject subset with variables = AEBODSYS, over_variables = TRUE, keeping only its '..ard_hierarchical_overall..' rows; the SOC subset with variables = AEBODSYS; the PT subset with variables = c(AEBODSYS, AEDECOD), include = AEDECOD. 4) table_plan(cols = c('TRT01A', 'AESEV'), ...) as in UAT-004, plan_levels(AESEV = c(MILD = 'Mild', MODERATE = 'Moderate', SEVERE = 'Severe')). 5) Give plan_col_header() two lines: the arm over its three severities. 6) Write the RTF and open it.
expected: Under each arm three columns Mild, Moderate, Severe; a subject is counted once in the any-TEAE row, once per SOC and once per PT, under the highest severity; the rows are SOC and PT as in UAT-004. Visual check.

steps: 1) From pharmaverseadam::adlb keep two parameters (for example ALT and AST), ANL01FL == 'Y' or ABLFL == 'Y', at Baseline, Week 12 and Week 24. 2) ard_summary() of AVAL, and of CHG after baseline, by PARAM, AVISIT and TRTA (N, mean, sd, median, min, max). 3) table_plan(cols = c('TRTA', 'variable'), rows = c(PARAM = 'PARAM', Visit = 'AVISIT')), plan_levels(variable = c('AVAL', 'CHG')), plan_stub(), plan_col_header() with the arm over Value and Change. 4) Write the RTF and open it.
expected: For each parameter and visit, n, Mean (SD), Median, Min, Max of the value and of the change under each arm; the change is empty at Baseline; the numbers equal an independent summary. Visual check.

steps: 1) From pharmaverseadam::adlb keep one parameter (for example ALT) at one post-baseline visit, one record per subject (ANL01FL == 'Y'). 2) Make BNRIND and ANRIND factors with levels c('LOW', 'NORMAL', 'HIGH'), so a category no subject has still shows. 3) ard_tabulate(adlb, by = c(TRTA, BNRIND), variables = ANRIND). 4) normalize_ard() |> table_plan(cols = c('TRTA', 'BNRIND'), rows = c(group = 'variable')) |> plan_cells(c(n == 0 ~ '0', '{n:.0f} ({p:.1f%})')) |> plan_levels(BNRIND = c(LOW = 'Low', NORMAL = 'Normal', HIGH = 'High'), ANRIND = c(LOW = 'Low', NORMAL = 'Normal', HIGH = 'High')), plan_col_header() with the arm over the baseline categories. 5) Write the RTF and open it.
expected: Under each arm the baseline categories Low, Normal, High in that order; the post-baseline categories down in the same order; each count equals table(BNRIND, ANRIND) in the arm, 0 where no subject (a baseline category with no subject too). Visual check.

steps: 1) Run the 'Vital signs by visit' example of the package's Gallery article (pharmaverseadam::advs, systolic and diastolic blood pressure). 2) Open t_vs.rtf.
expected: Each parameter is a block with its visits under it, a blank row between the blocks; under each arm Value and Change from baseline with n and Mean (SD); the header shows the arm's N. Visual check.

steps: 1) Run the code of the package's article 'A listing and its summary in one table: plan_append()' (fictional PK data). 2) Open the RTF.
expected: Each page holds one analyte and treatment: the subjects' concentrations by time point (BLQ where below the limit), then a blank row and the summary statistics (N, Mean, SD, CV%, ...) for the same group, under one column header. Visual check.

steps: 1) Run the 'Kaplan-Meier plot' example of the package's Gallery article (base R plot of survival::survfit() on pharmaverseadam data). 2) Open f_km.rtf.
expected: The plot is on one page at the size given, its titles in the header and its footnotes below; the curves and censoring marks are those the plot draws in R. Visual check.

steps: 1) Make a data frame of five subgroups with an estimate and its lower and upper limits (fictional numbers). 2) ggplot2: geom_pointrange() of the estimate by subgroup, a vertical line at 1, a log x axis. 3) rtf_document() |> rtf_figures(plot, titles = c('Figure 14.2.2', 'Hazard ratio by subgroup'), footnotes = 'Fictional data.') |> generate_rtfreport(file). 4) Open the RTF.
expected: The forest plot is on the page with the titles above and the footnote below; every subgroup and its interval show as in R. Visual check.

steps: 1) Write the company style once: st <- rtf_style(font = 'Times New Roman', font_size_half_points = 18L, title_format = 'table', titles = list(align = 'center'), footnotes = list(border = rtf_border(top = TRUE)), header = list(color = '#7F7F7F')). 2) Run the programs of UAT-001 and UAT-010 with rtf_document(style = st), their plans with plan_style(border = 'tfl'). 3) Run UAT-001 once more with plan_style(border = 'tfl', font = 'Courier New'). 4) Open the three RTFs.
expected: All use Times New Roman 9 pt and the table rules of the preset; the two UAT-001 files show their page header text in grey (UAT-010's program has no page header); UAT-010's titles are centred above and its footnotes have a rule above them; in the third file the table alone is in Courier New (the program's own setting wins). Visual check.

steps: 1) Run the program of UAT-001 with rtf_document(page = rtf_page(paper_size = 'A4', orientation = 'portrait', margin_top_in = 1, margin_bottom_in = 1, margin_left_in = 1, margin_right_in = 1)). 2) Open the RTF and Word's Page Setup.
expected: Page Setup shows A4, portrait, all four margins 1 inch (2.54 cm); the table fits within the margins.

steps: 1) Run the programs of UAT-001 and UAT-004 with 'Page {AUTO_PAGE} of {AUTO_TOTAL_PAGES}' in place of 'Page {PAGE} of {TOTAL_PAGES}', and the program of UAT-007 with a page header in place of plan_titles(): rtf_section(header = rtf_header(list(c(l = 'Protocol: CDISCPILOT01', r = 'Page {AUTO_PAGE} of {AUTO_TOTAL_PAGES}'), c('Listing 16.2.7'), c('Adverse events')))); write the three RTFs to one folder. 2) toc <- assemble_folder(dir) and look at it. 3) assemble_folder(dir, output_file = 'all.rtf'). 4) Open all.rtf, update the fields (Ctrl+A, F9).
expected: toc lists the two tables in table-number order (14.1.1, 14.3.1.2), then the listing (only a 'Table N' header line is read as a number); all.rtf starts with a table of contents whose entries go to their pages when clicked and show those pages' numbers; the pages are numbered through the whole document. Visual check.

steps: 1) Save the plot of UAT-008 as a PNG with ggplot2::ggsave(dpi = 300) and as an EMF (for example devEMF, or your graphics tool). 2) rtf_document() |> rtf_figures(list(rtfplot('fig.png'), rtfplot('fig.emf', width_twips = 8640L, height_twips = 5040L))) |> generate_rtfreport(file). 3) Open the RTF.
expected: Two pages: the PNG at the size its pixels and resolution give, the EMF at 6 x 3.5 inches and sharp when zoomed. Visual check.

steps: 1) In the program of UAT-001 give rtf_document(program = '/studies/XYZ-001/programs/tfl/t_dm.R') and keep '{PROGRAM_FULL}    Generated on: {DATETIME}' in the footer. 2) Run it. 3) Open the RTF and note the time it was run.
expected: Every page's footer shows the program path given, made absolute ({PROGRAM_FULL}: C:\studies\XYZ-001\programs\tfl\t_dm.R on Windows; {PROGRAM} prints it as given), and the date and time of the run (for example 02Nov2026  14:05), the same on every page. Visual check.
